items.label: A
items.critique: Tidy, logistical offer that explains the setup (crowd, refugees, bandits) and hands over a key with tactical advice in the reminder; Westwood's openings rarely justify themselves so neatly or give stealth tips.

items.label: B
items.critique: Short escort drop-off, breathless 'I must hurry and so should you!', 'You remain our only hope', and a chit-chat reminder: the hurried, slightly hokey Nox register.

items.label: C
items.critique: Stiff mentor diction ('transpiring', 'antiquated records', 'furnish the answers') and a real grammar slip ('incursions ... is on a steady rise') are characteristic of the shipped script; reminder names 'book and amulet' plainly.

items.label: D
items.critique: Stock idiom ('rest on laurels'), exclamations, 'Now, off with you!' and a terse journal line read like Westwood, though the plot summary is a little crowded.

items.label: E
items.critique: Clipped one-line pages, quirky 'heed its bite', 'Get a move on' reminder: odd, compact and characterful in the Nox way.

items.label: F
items.critique: Hard to parse: an introduction that strings titles together, a blade to be blessed, a kiln, then a two-page reminder with shouted 'YOU'; the reminder is longer and more emphatic than Westwood's usual one-liners.

items.label: G
items.critique: Atmospheric opener ('Dark days have come upon the crossroads'), shop pointer, double hyphen and a route-spelling journal ('Go north from X to Y and defeat Z') feel assembled from a template rather than spoken.

items.label: H
items.critique: Very plain, fragmentary directions ('You'll know. And careful.') and a reminder that redundantly repeats the task: the unpolished but authentic shipped feel.

items.label: I
items.critique: Exclamation on nearly every sentence, a missing-scout side detail and precise directions plus a return point read as a designer's brief voiced; same Ogres-in-the-watchtower kit as A and G.

items.label: J
items.critique: Overloaded with circumstantial detail (reeds, boatmen with torches, walkways, roofs, starving hamlets) and long run-on exclamations; Westwood keeps the stakes to one plain sentence.

tells: New texts over-explain the backstory with concrete scene detail (who fled where, who rowed in, which wall was climbed); Westwood states the task and stakes in one or two plain sentences.
New texts reuse a small kit of stock elements (north road, old watchtower, 'drive X out', Ogre brutes, caravans plundered) that makes them sound like siblings.
Westwood's lines have rough edges: grammar slips, stilted Latinate words in a mentor's mouth, fragments like 'You'll know. And careful.', redundant reminders; new texts are grammatically clean.
New journals spell out routes and objectives in full ('Go north from X to Y and defeat Z'); Westwood journals are terse ('Retrieve the X').
Westwood reminders are short and impatient ('Go! Don't just stand there.'); new reminders add fresh tactical advice or extra emphasis.
Overuse of exclamation marks on every sentence and double-hyphen dashes mark the new texts.
